title: Workflow — ScrumIA
meta_description: How a project runs end to end with the reference composition: brief, scoping, refinement, sprint, review. Each step names the module that carries it.
hero_title: A full run, end to end
hero_intro: The reference composition, step by step. Each step names the module behind it.
shape_diagram:
Human     │ brief, challenge, brainstorm
          ▼
discovery │ scoping → issues + branch carrying the specs
          ▼
tracker   │ refinement → Ready for dev, or sub-issues per context
   ↕      │   ↳ pulls in roles when their answer changes the ticket
team      │
          ▼
Human     │ signs off on designs that are doubtful, critical or risky
          ▼
team      │ manager builds the sprint with the team → To dev
          ▼
team      │ dynamic workflows: implementation, review, QA
   ↕      │   ↳ implementation follows the app's own module
impl      │     and the practices plugged into the app
          ▼
Human     │ review PR, test → Done
step1_p1: An idea, a problem, a hunch. Scoping pushes back: does the problem exist? does this solve it? what becomes impossible? where are the edge cases? what is assumed but unsaid?
step1_p2: The one point where sustained human attention pays — and where it costs least.
step2_title: Scoping produces issues and a specs branch
step2_p1: Business features first, then app features — one per app, never two. Then the issues.
step2_p2: Specs ship on a specs/<slug> branch in an open PR: design gets reviewed in the same tool as code, and refinement starts from something fixed rather than a remembered conversation.
step3_li1: A feature it belongs to exists and is current
step3_li2: Acceptance criteria are written, identified AC-n, and can fail
step3_li3: The blast radius is known: which apps, which files
step3_li4: No open question blocks the start
step3_p2: Roles with the wider view get pulled in when their answer changes the ticket — not to rubber-stamp it. The ticket may split into sub-issues by context: one per app, since the implementation context differs.
step4_title: A human signs off where it matters
step4_p1: Escalated: a business rule had to be invented, the split changed the ask, the ticket is wide-reaching, or a role raised a reservation. Everything else moves to Ready for dev on its own.
step5_p1: A batch of tickets that don't collide — two tickets on the same files either serialise or merge. The human approves the batch explicitly.
step6_p1: One workflow per ticket, in parallel, each in its own worktree. Each gets a ticket number and nothing else — it loads its own context.
step6_li1: Load context through the specs module
step6_li2: Update the spec before the code, if behaviour changes
step6_li3: Implement following the app's implementation module and its practices — specific beats generic
step6_li4: Cover each AC-n with a test that can fail
step6_li5: Self-review, then role review based on blast radius
step7_p1: The PR carries the criterion-by-criterion mapping, the specs it changed, review verdicts, and open reservations with their issues. Agents don't merge, except for categories explicitly listed in config.
spec_note_p: Writing the spec first surfaces contradictions before they get encoded — where fixing them is cheapest. If one shows up against another feature, execution stops and asks the business role. It never settles a rule on its own: a rule invented mid-flight becomes everyone's reference without anyone having decided it.
gates_intro: Validation cost tracks risk, rather than being uniform.
gates_r2_when: Routed by the actual diff, not the declared label.
gates_note_p: The disagreement is passed through as-is, not blended into an average. It's precisely the case that needs a human call — smoothing it destroys the signal.
auto_intro: An explicit setting in .scrumia/config.yaml, not an implicit property.
auto_c1: # a PR touching documentation and nothing else
auto_note_p: auto_merge is a single setting for the whole project, not a per-category list: none (nothing merges unattended, the default), docs-only (a PR touching documentation and nothing else), or all.
human1_desc: The AI challenges and proposes; the human settles the blocking points.
human2_desc: Where doubt, criticality or risk warrant it.
human3_desc: Launching a sprint is a decision, not a consequence.
human4_desc: The final call, unless a category is explicitly delegated.
human_p: Everywhere else, agents move on their own. If you find yourself doing something else, that's a signal about the composition — not about your discipline.
human_note_title: On "prepare the next sprint while this one runs"
human_note_p: Not automatable within one session: a subagent can't spawn subagents, and agent teams are experimental with one team per session. Two Claude Code sessions on the same repo get you there — one consuming the current sprint, one refining the next. Since state lives in the tracker rather than in session memory, they stay consistent without coordinating.
